claim: Evo 2 7B was trained on 2.4 trillion tokens and Evo 2 40B on 9.3 trillion tokens
quote: We trained two versions of Evo 2: a smaller version with 7 billion parameters trained on 2.4 trillion tokens (Evo 2 7B), and a larger version with 40 billion parameters trained on 9.3 trillion tokens (Evo 2 40B).

claim: OpenGenome2 holds more than 8.8 trillion nucleotides from bacteria, archaea, eukarya and bacteriophage
quote: compiled from curated, non-redundant nucleotide sequence data with a total of more than 8.8 trillion nucleotides from bacteria, archaea, eukarya and bacteriophage

claim: Training ran in two phases: pretraining at 8,192-token context weighted to genic windows, then midtraining extending context to 1 million tokens
quote: Our first stage of pretraining uses a context length of 8,192 tokens, with data weighting focused on genic windows to learn functional genetic elements, followed by a multi-stage midtraining phase over which we extend the context length of Evo 2 to 1 million tokens to learn the relationships between elements across long genomic distances

claim: Genomes of eukaryote-infecting viruses were excluded for biosafety, verified by high perplexity on eukaryotic viral genomes
quote: As in Evo 1, we excluded genomic sequences from viruses that infect eukaryotic hosts from the training data for biosafety purposes. We verified that these data exclusions led to high perplexity on genomic sequences from eukaryotic viruses

claim: StripedHyena 2 gives up to a 3x speedup at 1 million context and 40B parameters over optimized Transformer baselines
quote: StripedHyena 2 provides substantially higher throughput (at 40 billion parameters, up to 3× speedup at 1 million context length) than highly optimized Transformer6 baselines

claim: StripedHyena 2 also improves DNA loss scaling over both Transformers and StripedHyena 1
quote: StripedHyena 2 also improves loss scaling on DNA against both Transformers and StripedHyena 1

claim: Needle-in-a-haystack: Evo 2 recovers a specific 100 bp sequence hidden in 1 million bp of random DNA
quote: Evo 2 can identify and predict the value of a specific 100 base pair sequence (the needle) hidden within 1 million base pairs of random DNA (the haystack)

claim: Midtraining loss improved with both model scale and longer context
quote: multi-stage extension phase, which showed improvements in loss with both model scale and longer context

claim: SNVs near start codons produced strong likelihood changes, then a three-base periodicity with wobble positions least impactful
quote: This was followed by a three-base periodicity pattern reflecting the triplet codons, with changes at the wobble positions showing lower impact on likelihood.

claim: Upstream likelihood patterns matched the Shine-Dalgarno sequence in prokaryotes and the Kozak sequence in eukaryotes
quote: namely, the Shine–Dalgarno sequence17 for prokaryotes and the Kozak sequence18 for eukaryotes

claim: Across 20 prokaryotic and 16 eukaryotic species, non-synonymous, premature-stop and frameshift mutations changed likelihood far more than synonymous ones
quote: Non-synonymous mutations, premature stop codons and frameshift mutations caused much larger changes in likelihood than synonymous mutations.

claim: tRNA and rRNA deletions had much larger likelihood effects than intergenic or other noncoding deletions
quote: deletions in transfer RNAs (tRNAs) and ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs) had much larger effects than deletions in intergenic and other noncoding loci

claim: The 40B model was more sensitive than 7B to miRNA and snoRNA deletions
quote: The 40B model exhibited higher sensitivity to deletions in microRNA (miRNA) and small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA) sequences compared with the 7B model.

claim: Evo 2 assigned lower likelihoods to less efficiently translated codons
quote: Evo 2 also predicted that less efficiently translated codons had lower likelihoods than more efficient codons

claim: Evo 2 distinguished the standard, mycoplasma (Code 4) and ciliate (Code 6) genetic codes
quote: the model learned the difference between the standard code (stop codons TAA, TAG and TGA), the mycoplasma code (Code 4, stop codons TAA and TAG) and the ciliate code (Code 6, stop codon TGA)

claim: Recoding ciliate genomes to the standard code made standard stop mutations read as deleterious, showing context-dependent code inference
quote: When ciliate genomes were artificially recoded to the standard genetic code, Evo 2 predicted mutations from the standard stop codons as deleterious, demonstrating that the model relies on sequence context to determine the appropriate genetic code

claim: On DMS, Evo 2 is competitive with ProGen for protein and RNA language models for ncRNA, but underperforms state-of-the-art protein DMS models
quote: Evo 2 is competitive with widely used ProGen language models for protein DMS and with RNA language models for ncRNA DMS, although it underperforms state-of-the-art models on protein DMS.

claim: Fitness-prediction performance begins to saturate and can decrease at the largest model scales
quote: the performance of Evo 2 on these fitness prediction benchmarks begins to saturate and can decrease at the largest model scales

claim: No correlation was found between Evo 2 likelihood and human-virus protein fitness, consistent with the data exclusions
quote: We found no correlation between Evo 2 likelihood and viral protein fitness

claim: Exon classifiers on Evo 2 7B embeddings reached AUROC 0.91-0.99 on eight held-out species, beating Nucleotide Transformer, Evo 1, GC content and PhyloP
quote: our best classifier achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) ranging from 0.91 to 0.99 (Fig. 2h,i), outperforming models trained on embeddings from other genomic language models, Nucleotide Transformer22 and Evo 1 (ref. 1), and classification by conservation metrics (local GC content and PhyloP)

claim: The classifier beat AUGUSTUS on every species, and SegmentNT on all species outside SegmentNT's training set plus one of the three inside it
quote: outperforms ab initio AUGUSTUS23 across all species tested. Evo 2 also outperforms SegmentNT24 on all species outside the SegmentNT training set and on one of the three species in its training set.

claim: On prokaryotic/archaeal/phage gene essentiality Evo 2 performed similarly to Evo 1 and better than other zero-shot methods
quote: we found that Evo 2 models performed similarly to Evo 1 and better than other zero-shot methods in predicting gene essentiality across diverse species

claim: Human gene essentiality: Evo 2 40B reached AUROC 0.66/AUPRC 0.15, above other genomic language models and within the PhyloP range, but modest overall
quote: Evo 2 40B (AUROC = 0.66, area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) = 0.15) outperformed other genomic language models (AUROC range 0.50– 0.59, AUPRC range 0.09–0.12) and performs within the range of four PhyloP conservation scores (AUROC range 0.65–0.71, AUPRC range 0.13–0.21)

claim: ClinVar coding SNVs: Evo 2 was ahead of zero-shot methods including ESM-2 but behind ESM-1b, GPN-MSA and some PhyloP variants
quote: For coding region SNVs, the 40B and 7B models performed competitively, ahead of zero-shot methods, including ESM-2, but behind ESM-1b, GPN-MSA and some PhyloP variants

claim: ClinVar coding non-SNVs: both Evo 2 models beat every other method, and leading models such as AlphaMissense and GPN-MSA cannot score them at all
quote: both Evo 2 models outperformed all other methods; notably, these non-SNV variants are not possible to score by leading models such as AlphaMissense and GPN-MSA

claim: Noncoding SNVs: Evo 2 40B ranked first among unsupervised models and only trailed supervised ones; on noncoding non-SNVs it beat everything tested
quote: For noncoding SNVs, Evo 2 40B ranked first among unsupervised models and only trailed behind supervised models (Fig. 3c). For noncoding non-SNVs, Evo 2 40B outperformed all models tested

claim: SpliceVarDB: Evo 2 ranked first among unsupervised models on exonic and intronic variants; intronic was competitive with supervised models, trailing SpliceAI and CADD but ahead of Pangolin
quote: On intronic variants, zero-shot prediction with Evo 2 was competitive with supervised models, slightly trailing SpliceAI and CADD but ahead of Pangolin

claim: BRCA1: Evo 2 was strong on coding SNVs and outperformed all other models on noncoding SNVs
quote: Zero-shot prediction with Evo 2 exhibited strong performance on coding SNVs and outperformed all other models on BRCA1 noncoding SNVs

claim: BRCA2: Evo 2 surpassed GPN-MSA and came second behind the supervised CADD
quote: Evo 2 surpassed specialized models such as GPN-MSA when predicting coding and noncoding variants together, achieving second-best performance behind CADD, a supervised model

claim: A ridge regression on Evo 2 embeddings beat zero-shot 40B on the BRCA1 test set, reaching AUROC 0.95 and AUPRC 0.88
quote: outperforming zero-shot prediction by Evo 2 40B on the test set (AUROC = 0.95, AUPRC = 0.88)

claim: DART-eval: Evo 2 40B beat other unsupervised models (caQTL AUROC 0.58, dsQTL 0.66) but trailed ChromBPNet (0.77, 0.89)
quote: Evo 2 40B (chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTL) AUROC = 0.58, DNase I sensitivity quantitative trait loci (dsQTL) AUROC = 0.66) outperforms other unsupervised

claim: Evo 2 trails supervised models for distal regulatory variants despite leading on non-SNVs
quote: maintains this performance even in the absence of strong site-independent sequence conservation, although it falls behind supervised models for distal regulatory variants

claim: Evo 2 is not trained on any human genetic variation or functional genomics data
quote: Notably, Evo 2 is not trained on any human genetic variation or functional genomics data.

claim: A Batch-TopK sparse autoencoder was trained on layer-26 representations using 1 billion tokens
quote: We trained a Batch-TopK SAE32 on Evo 2 representations from layer 26 (Methods). The SAE was trained on representations from 1 billion tokens

claim: Feature f/19746 activates on annotated prophages including the cryptic prophage CPZ-55 in E. coli
quote: Feature f/19746 is closely associated with prophage regions across prokaryotes (Extended Data Fig. 7b) and activates on annotated prophages in the Escherichia coli genome, including the cryptic prophage CPZ-55

claim: The same feature fires on CRISPR spacers and on scrambled synthetic spacers, implying learned association rather than memorized phage genomes
quote: as well as after the last CRISPR direct repeat and on synthetic, scrambled spacer sequences, suggesting that Evo 2 associates CRISPR spacers with phage sequences as opposed to directly memorizing phage genomes

claim: Features were found for ORFs, intergenic regions, tRNAs and rRNAs, and for protein secondary structures such as alpha-helices and beta-sheets
quote: We further probed for structural signatures at the protein level and identified features linked to protein secondary structures, such as α-helices and β-sheets

claim: Feature f/24278 preferentially activates on frameshifts and premature stop mutations
quote: we identified a mutation-sensitive feature (f/24278) that preferentially activates on frameshifts and pre-mature stop mutations

claim: Unsupervised SAE features hit 70% of promoter-enriched HOCOMOCO motifs, against HOMER's 35% recall
quote: Evo 2 unsupervised SAE features have significant hits (q < 0.01, Sandelin–Wasserman similarity) to 70%

claim: HOMER, a specialized motif discovery algorithm, recalled only 35% of the same motifs
quote: a specialized motif discovery algorithm, only recalls 35% of the same motifs

claim: Exon-boundary features f/1050 and f/25666 mark the first base after an intron and the last base before one; the coding feature also fires on bacterial ORFs
quote: the first bases of an exon following an intron (f/1050), and the last base of an exon followed by an intron (f/25666)

claim: SAE features trained only on model organisms transferred to a genic region of the woolly mammoth genome
quote: we further observed that these features transferred to a genic region within a portion of the woolly mammoth genome37

claim: Gene completion across six species from a 1,000 bp upstream plus 500-1,000 bp gene prompt gave high amino acid recovery that improved with scale and beat Evo 1
quote: We found that Evo 2 achieves gene completion with high amino acid sequence recovery, which improved with scale (Fig. 5b).

claim: Even when directly elicited, Evo 2 had essentially random sequence recovery for human viral proteins
quote: Even when directly trying to elicit a viral protein, Evo 2 had essentially random performance in sequence recovery, preventing Evo 2 from unconstrained or accidental generation of human viral proteins.

claim: Over 250 unique 16-kb mitochondrial sequences carried the correct number of CDSs, tRNA genes and rRNA genes and kept proper synteny
quote: generating over 250 unique 16-kb sequences (Methods). When annotated with MitoZ38, we found that the generated sequences have the correct number of CDSs, tRNA genes and rRNA genes expected in human mitochondria

claim: Generated mitochondrial codon usage closely matched the human mitochondrial genome and one of each expected tRNA was produced
quote: The codon usage of generated sequences also closely matched that of the human mitochondrial genome

claim: Ten 580-kb M. genitalium-scale sequences were generated from a 10.5-kb prompt; nearly 70% of generated genes had significant Pfam hits against Evo 1 131k's 18%
quote: Nearly 70% of generated genes contained significant Pfam hits, a substantial improvement over Evo 1 131k (18%)

claim: Generated protein length and secondary structure distributions resembled natural M. genitalium, but structure prediction confidences were lower
quote: The length and secondary structure distributions of generated proteins resemble natural M. genitalium distributions

claim: Yeast: twenty 330-kb sequences from a 10.5-kb chromosome III prompt; tRNA and gene density fell below the native genome while gene lengths matched
quote: The density of tRNA and gene features was below those found in the native yeast genome

claim: Genome-scale generations are not guaranteed functional or replication-competent and lack some essential genes
quote: these evaluation metrics do not guarantee functional or replication-competent genomes, and our genome-scale generations lack important elements, such as some essential genes

claim: Chromatin design used an Enformer and Borzoi ensemble as the scoring function, with a beam search re-evaluating every 128 bp of generated sequence
quote: Instead of sampling and scoring full, multi-kilobase designs, we conducted a beam search that re-evaluates Enformer and Borzoi after each new 128 bp of sampled sequence and only continues autoregressive generation off of the most promising samples

claim: Design quality rose log-linearly with beam search width, that is, with inference-time compute
quote: we observed a log-linear relationship in which increasing the beam search width—thereby increasing inference-time compute—resulted in better-quality designs

claim: Sampling 30 or more 128-bp chunks and keeping the top two at each beam step sufficed
quote: Sampling 30 or more 128-bp chunks and selecting the top two chunks at each step of the beam search was sufficient to achieve final designs

claim: Three Morse code messages written into the epigenome of mouse embryonic stem cells gave experimental ATAC-seq AUROCs of 0.92-0.95
quote: The three Morse code patterns had good agreement between the predicted and experimentally measured chromatin profiles, with the experimental patterns having AUROCs of 0.92–0.95

claim: The designed messages were 'LO', 'ARC' and 'EVO2'
quote: Our designed messages include “LO” (the first message transmitted over the Internet and the first word in Edmund Spenser’s The Faerie Queene), “ARC” (the name of the research institute in which this design was conducted), and “EVO2”.

claim: Replacing Evo 2 with a uniform or bigram proposal gave poorer token-matched inference-time scaling and poor ensemble consensus, suggesting adversarial samples
quote: with a uniform or bigram proposal replacing Evo 2, we observed poorer token-matched inference-time scaling and poor consensus among ensemble predictions

claim: Designed peak regions carried significantly higher predicted transcription factor motif density than non-peak regions (P = 3.6e-7)
quote: designed peak regions contain significantly higher predicted transcription factor motif density than non-peak regions (two-sided Welch’s t-test, P = 3.6 × 10−7)

claim: Unlike unigram or bigram designs, Evo 2 designs were enriched for transcription factors expressed in mESCs (P = 2.0e-4) despite no explicit conditioning for motifs
quote: Evo 2 designs were significantly enriched for transcription factors expressed in mESCs (one-sided hypergeometric P = 2.0 × 10−4)

claim: Varying accessibility within a designed sequence succeeded in 33 of 36 designs (92%) with AUROC above 0.8 across HEK293T and K562
quote: We observed strong experimental success rates when we varied the level of chromatin accessibility within a designed sequence, with 33 out of 36 designs (92%) having an AUROC greater than 0.8

claim: Designing differential accessibility between two cell types was much harder: 4 of 24 designs (17%) exceeded twofold and 1 of 24 (4%) exceeded threefold
quote: we observed that 4 out of 24 of these designs (17%) had greater than twofold differential accessibility, and 1 out of 24 designs (4%) had greater than threefold differential accessibility

claim: In the four >2-fold designs the peak motifs were enriched for K562-expressed transcription factors (P = 0.0017) but not HEK293T-expressed ones (P = 0.25)
quote: the predicted transcription factor motifs in the design peaks were significantly enriched for K562-expressed transcription factors (one-sided hypergeometric P = 0.0017)

claim: The 40B 1M-context model performs best overall, the 7B 1M-context model is competitive for lightweight inference, and the experimental 1B short-context release should be avoided
quote: The Evo 2 40B 1 million (1M)-context model demonstrates best overall performance, though the 7B 1M-context model is competitive and useful for settings requiring lightweight inference.

claim: Task-specific post-training may circumvent the viral data-exclusion mitigation and should be approached with caution
quote: Task-specific post-training may circumvent this risk mitigation measure and should be approached with caution.

claim: Red teaming meant to elicit pathogenic human viral proteins showed generations were effectively random in that domain
quote: Probing and testing these measures by red teaming meant to directly elicit pathogenic human viral proteins showed generations were effectively random in this domain

claim: The population-free design of Evo 2 mitigated ancestry biases in model predictions
quote: mitigated ancestry biases in model predictions55 (Extended Data Fig. 2d)

claim: Improving generation with inference-time guidance can require computationally intensive sampling
quote: Improving generation with inference-time guidance can notably require computationally intensive sampling.
